title: P2W to the extreme Whales rule
content: I play this game on my tablet. I gave it two stars because of the graphics and gameplay. It’s a great game if only you didn’t have to pay a lot just to enjoy the game. If you find a fun alliance that dominates a faction, it can be fun. Even without paying because you can play the role of pather or support. But some aspects of the game make it hard to have fun without paying. The egg hatching to power up your dragon is fun. But even when you pay a good amount of money, the probability of something meaningful is infinitely small. It’s like gambling. There’s a pity award but it rarely makes a dent in your power compared to others.  I’m not saying make it cheap to win, but you made it extremely expensive. To the point where I was willing to pay $5 or $10 here and there until I realized that I get barely anything for it. The egg probability game means you could spend >$100 a month and still feel powerless compared to even upper average players. In the second reign, there was a closed alliance that dominated the faction. As outsiders, we have 0 knowledge of their plans and feel irrelevant. And the two other factions ganged up on us. So >$200 and still weak, irrelevant, lost, no purpose. Maybe if there was a pve mode where you didn’t need to engage in territory grabs, it would have been fun for people that don’t want to deal with social drama while still playing with dragons.

You can spend tons of money and hope to get enough states to upgrade to 6+, but that initial offer is it. It won’t even cycle back through in season 2+. 
So, you play, then you like it, then you think - I’ll spend some money. But then after you spend it you realize you missed the boat and have an expensive but terrible account. 
You go to the discord to suggest changes, and the zealots there say, “you should have asked us here before buying” 
I’m sorry I downloaded a game to play a game, not to have to be on discord, WhatsApp and every other app at the same time as I am trying to play the game - all on one phone.

I’m over this money pit. It was started and killed in 3 months for me over 2 seasons. 
Thanks for the memories

author: Alpha Corndog
title: Beware!
content:
I have spent hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars playing this game since launch but when I voiced my concerns on the game’s official discord server, I was banned. Before you jump to conclusions as to why, know that I did not use hateful, derogatory, obscene, or otherwise threatening language when I shared my thoughts. In fact, I shared my feedback on the reign transition channel which was created for feedback from players transitioning into a new reign. I simply stated the obvious issues I personally observed in the game and pointed out that they had not addressed those issues despite their contradictory statements that they had. They (whoever moderates the discord server) decided to take it personally and ban my account from the server.

What are the issues you ask?

1. You can’t play with your friends after the first reign, as the development team disabled using friends codes to invite others into your game server. You can do it in the first reign, but after that it’s disabled.

2. When a new reign starts, your alliance is merged in with other alliances/factions from multiple game servers. I immediately saw a gross imbalance in player power after the merge, as multiple players were already at 2 million or more power in less than 24 hours of starting the new reign - it’s quite obvious those players purchased their way to the top overnight. I understand this game is “pay to win” like most mobile games these days. But if players purchase the maximum on a daily basis then they are far above any real competition in the game. They are basically unstoppable and no one can compete with them. Subsequently, the game is no longer fun to play when you are faced with such opponents. It’s discouraging for players like myself who spend moderately to play. You really need to establish some sort of power tiering system to group players into servers that closely match their purchasing power. 

3. Bugs, glitches, crashing, freezing, and all of the above are frequent in this game. I know it’s a relatively new game and not perfect but the issues I see have long gone unaddressed. Everything from resource counters being incorrect, to delays in campaign progress appearing. I could go on, but it’s too much to list. Just know there are technical issues galore.

So with that said, they can ban me from the discord, but they can’t ban me here and I hope others find this to be an informative deterrent. I have personally stopped all in game spending until major improvements are made. I would suggest others do the same to make their voice heard. If we all choke their revenue stream, perhaps they will get the message.

author: rpchris
title: A Cynical Pay-to-Win Cash Grab Wearing a Game of Thrones Costume
content:
This game is little more than a Game of Thrones-themed variation of *Underground Fortress*, built around the same tired formula: start players off with quick progress, gradually starve them of resources, and then relentlessly pressure them to spend money.

At first, the game seems harmless enough. You collect resources, build your castle, improve your skills, and raise dragons. Progress is fast, rewards arrive frequently, and the game creates the illusion that strategy and consistent play will be enough to succeed.

That illusion does not last long.

Eventually, progress slows to a crawl because the game deliberately stops providing enough resources to advance at a reasonable pace. Conveniently, the store is always ready to sell you exactly what you are missing. This is not a side feature or an optional shortcut—it is the entire business model.

Even spending money is not enough. To remain competitive, you must join an alliance, which often comes with daily participation requirements, minimum power levels, mandatory event involvement, and constant expectations to keep progressing. Meeting those requirements becomes nearly impossible unless you are willing to spend an absurd amount of time in the game, an absurd amount of money, or both.

Then there are the server whales: players with overwhelmingly powerful armies, maxed-out skills, and capabilities that ordinary players have virtually no chance of matching. Whether they are independently spending fortunes or receiving some form of promotional support, their presence serves an obvious purpose. They create a permission structure that encourages everyone else to spend more just to compete—or risk having weeks of progress reduced to ash in one-sided PvP battles.

There is no meaningful finish line. Even after reaching a high tier, your position may last only a few days before another event, upgrade system, resource shortage, or power increase pressures you to spend again. The game does not reward achievement; it continually devalues it so that it can sell it back to you.

Without PvP, there is very little here. The gameplay is repetitive, the storyline is dull, and the Game of Thrones setting feels more like expensive branding pasted over a generic mobile strategy game than a meaningful part of the experience.

This is not a strategy game with optional purchases. It is a monetization system disguised as a game. Its real objective is not to entertain players, but to frustrate, pressure, and manipulate them into spending increasingly large amounts of money.

Avoid it. Your time, your money, and your patience deserve better.

author: Dompot_camiloza
title: Great, but a GLARING FLAW
content:
I’ve really enjoyed playing Game of Thrones: Dragonfire. The graphics are great, the dragon mechanics are fun, and the alliance and kingdom warfare make for an engaging strategy game. It’s one of the better mobile strategy games I’ve played.
That said, there’s one major gameplay issue that I hope the developers address. Players occupying an SOP can abuse the Resolve mechanic by sending a march to attack a Resolve-protected opponent and then instantly recalling their march. This allows them to avoid incoming attacks while still reaching and hitting enemy siege marches. Since attacking an SOP is already very difficult, this tactic creates an unfair advantage with very little counterplay. Especially when you can potentially perform that trick 30 times vs an attacking player only having 10 APs for 1 march. 
Strategy games should reward planning and skill, not exploits that are nearly impossible to counter. I hope the developers review this interaction and make adjustments so that battles are decided by strategy rather than loopholes in the mechanics.
Overall, I still think this is a fantastic game and would recommend it, but fixing this issue would make kingdom warfare much more balanced and enjoyable.

author: Siccor30
title: A Beautiful Idea Held Back by a Shallow Experience
content:
As a huge Game of Thrones fan, I expected this game to capture the scale, freedom, and excitement of the world of Westeros. Instead, it feels like a very basic mobile strategy game with a Game of Thrones skin. The visuals are decent, but the gameplay lacks the depth and immersion this franchise deserves.

The biggest issue is that everything feels too restricted. The world should feel alive and interactive, but instead it feels like you’re constantly tapping menus and waiting on timers. A Game of Thrones game should feel epic—not like a budget city builder.

Here are some features that would dramatically improve the experience:

• Expand dragon progression. Let players purchase Dragon Keys, Dragon XP, evolution materials, and other resources directly from the shop. If players want to invest money into strengthening their dragons, give them meaningful ways to do it.

• Completely overhaul alliance chat. Communication feels outdated. Add:

* Emoji support
* Replying to messages
* Message reactions
* Ability to delete your own messages
* Pinned announcements
* Search function
* Shared battle reports
* Shared scouting reports
* Coordinate sharing
* Screenshot sharing

• More player freedom. Let us interact with the world more instead of constantly navigating menus. Exploration, events, and movement should feel dynamic rather than automated.

• Better social tools. Alliance leaders should be able to organize members more efficiently with announcements, polls, event scheduling, and improved role management.

• More PvE content. Add dragon hunts, world bosses, castle raids, expeditions, story missions, and seasonal events so there’s always something meaningful to do outside of PvP.

• Improve the shop. Right now it feels limited. Offer more optional progression items, customization, dragon cosmetics, castle themes, banners, portraits, and quality-of-life bundles.

• Alliance cooperation. Add alliance trading, resource donations, alliance quests, dragon training events, and shared objectives that actually make teamwork rewarding.

• Better customization. Let players personalize castles, dragons, banners, marches, profile cards, and animations.

The Game of Thrones universe is one of the richest fantasy worlds ever created. This game has a solid foundation, but right now it doesn’t match the scale or excitement of the source material. It feels like a generic kingdom builder instead of an unforgettable Game of Thrones experience.

I genuinely hope the developers continue improving it because this game has the potential to become something incredible. Right now, though, it feels more like a missed opportunity than the epic adventure fans were hoping for.

author: Gen X Casual Gamer
title: Pay to Play
content:
I’ve been a Game of Thrones fan for years, and Dragonfire has a lot of potential. The dragon designs, collecting system, and alliance gameplay are fun at first, but progression quickly becomes dominated by spending money.

If you’re willing to spend heavily, you’ll stay competitive. If you’re a casual or low-spending player, you’ll constantly find yourself falling behind players who can simply buy power. Events, dragon upgrades, and PvP rankings often feel more dependent on your wallet than your strategy.

The game itself is enjoyable, and the artwork and theme are excellent, but the pay-to-win mechanics make it difficult to recommend for long-term play. Free-to-play players should understand what they’re getting into before investing significant time.

Rating: 2/5 – Great Game of Thrones atmosphere, but progression and competitiveness are too heavily tied to spending.

author: Abraham Canche
title: Dear developers
content:
Since dragons are the absolute main focus and primary troop of this game, I’d love to see much deeper investment in them so they feel truly central and versatile.
Right now, I want to use dragons in many different ways: both as powerful carriers with troops assigned to them, and as independent strike forces. Let me send pure dragon groups to attack enemy castles, troops, or rival dragons without any ground units attached.
When dragons aren’t on campaign, it would be amazing to see them visibly living around my castle — smaller dragons flying patrols, circling overhead, or landing on towers and rooftops. That kind of life and atmosphere would make the game feel so much more immersive.
The dragon cave built into the castle should also feel like a real hub. I’d love to see dragons visibly entering and exiting the cave whenever troops are deployed or returning home.
Because dragons are the heart of this game, I really expect a wide variety of gameplay options and interactions with them. Little details matter a lot to me — things like realism and believable behaviors. For example, when ground troops are attached to dragons, it currently feels unrealistic that the troops walk straight over mountains. Instead, those combined forces should realistically have to travel around mountains, while pure dragon groups can fly straight over them. It would also be fantastic if I could hide pure dragon raids in mountain caves for ambushes or safe resting.
Pure dragon forces could also benefit from altitude-based tactics, such as scouting distant threats from high above or executing dive-bomb fire attacks that ground troops can’t replicate. This would make choosing between mixed armies and dragon-only strikes feel like a real strategic decision with meaningful trade-offs.
Let dragons show personality and growth over time. As they level up or participate in battles, they could develop unique traits — like increased fire range, faster flight endurance, or even minor behavioral quirks. This would make each dragon feel like a living companion rather than just a troop count.
Environmental storytelling would add incredible immersion: dragons leaving scorched landing spots or melted snow on rooftops, reacting to battles by circling excitedly overhead, or seeking shelter in storms. Give us more control over dragon behavior in downtime, like setting patrol routes around the castle or assigning specific dragons to guard key structures.
For realism in logistics, pure dragon groups should have advantages like faster map traversal and the ability to take shortcuts through impassable terrain, but with risks such as fatigue if overused. A small but powerful touch: dynamic camera moments when dragons launch or return a quick cinematic fly-through of the cave or a sweeping aerial view of the castle would make every march feel epic. Some short cinemátics which could be toggled on or off in setting for the dragons would be a nice touch aswell ❤️

author: Gamer3475
title: Wish it was better
content:
The gameplay loop just isn’t there for me. Nothing is permanent, all progress resets every 8 weeks or so at the end of a reign. Why would I bother spending time upgrading my stronghold and raising my dragons if everything is going to constantly reset. 

The whole faction and alliance aspect is also very underbaked, confusing, and never really explained. 

The game advertises raising dragons because that sells well but the dragons have very little to actually do with the game. 

I wish the game would not have done this stupid reign/faction/alliance thing. It would be so much better as a more traditional hero collector game where the heroes are dragons. Make the dragons front and center. Let us actually control our dragons in battle. That would be a much better game than this mess they’ve released instead.

author: Utopian Thoughts
title: Poorly thought out early game experience ruined this game.
content:
Joined an alliance day one, initial game was promising, and I figured out how to attack and was able to take 4 of my alliances 8 towns in the opening days. 

Now I login, I’m no longer on my team. My towns are no longer accessible to me.

Without the established relationships of GoTC and ability to “take my ball with me” I can be kicked by an abusive player and all my hard work down the drain with no recourse.

I will post aggressively about this in all venues and create songs lambasting this game if this isn’t addressed promptly. 

Abusive behavior by players and teams has ruined this game for me if what I worked for isn’t restored to me.

title: Terrible design choices
content: I wanted to love this game so much. Love the IP, but the developers made some stunningly bad design decisions. Can’t relocate in early game stages because there is no faction territory. Can join alliances but not leave them after you realize you can’t move near them. You can’t attack other tiles so people are essentially blocking you in. Have the developer never played these types of 4x or PvP based strategy games? Who the heck did they make this for? GoT fans who have never played this type of mobile strategy games? I am completely confused and off put by this game.
